From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up on logging / redaction requirements

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + a few follow-ups from our security team:

- We need clarity on what is logged by default for hosted inference (request/response bodies, headers, trace IDs, etc.).
- Our policy requires PII to be redacted before it is stored in any logs. We prefer server-side redaction but may also perform client-side masking.
- Retention: 90 days for any request/response logs that contain business data.
- Data residency: logs must be stored in the US region only.
- We may need SOC 2–aligned evidence for how logs are protected and redaction is implemented.

Can you confirm how Redwood handles request/response logging, header preservation, and trace IDs? Any example of redaction configuration or a sample redacted log would be super helpful.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Chen
Head of Security, FinTechCo

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@fintechco.com>
Cc: Bob Nguyen <bob.nguyen@fintechco.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up on logging / redaction requirements

Hi Alice —

Great talking earlier — appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front, details below:

1) Default logging (hosted API): minimal operational metadata only (request size, model used, latency, error codes). We do NOT persist full request/response payloads by default on the hosted plan.

2) Optional full request/response logging: available for Dedicated and Private deployments or by explicit opt-in for hosted customers under a data-processing addendum. When enabled, logs are written to customer-scoped, encrypted storage and can be configured for retention.

3) Redaction: Redwood supports server-side redaction rules applied before any write to persistent logs. Rules are pattern-based (regex), with support for named groups, replacement tokens, hashing (SHA256), and allowlists for headers. We recommend a dual approach: client-side masking for known PII and server-side rules for catch-all.

4) Trace IDs & headers: Trace IDs can be hashed or truncated before storage. Headers are handled with an allowlist/blocklist model — default is to block all non-essential headers and allow only request-id, user-agent, and x-forwarded-for (if you require).

5) Retention & residency: Retention is configurable; we can set lifecycle rules to purge logs after 90 days. Storage location for Dedicated/Private can be restricted to US-only regions. For hosted customers we can map logs to US regions if required under contract.

6) Security controls / SOC 2: logs are encrypted at rest with AES-256 and keys are KMS-managed; access is role-based and audited. We can provide a SOC 2–focused evidence pack (controls mapping + sample config) — attached is a short summary.

Next steps I propose:
- I attached two files: a quick redaction requirements doc and a sample redaction config YAML.
- Looping in Dev (Dev Patel) for a short technical note on the exact regex samples and how trace IDs are hashed.
- If that looks good, we can schedule a 30-min technical follow-up to walk through enabling this on your Dedicated instance.

Please see inline answers below to your specific asks.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redaction_config_example.yaml (YAML)]

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@fintechco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up on logging / redaction requirements — technical details

Hi Alice / Marissa —

Thanks for the summary — a few technical details you can share with your security team:

- Logging modes: log_level = {none | minimal | full}.
  - minimal: only telemetry (latency, model, request_size, error_code). No request/response body stored.
  - full: request and response bodies stored (subject to redaction rules).

- Redaction pipeline (applied server-side, pre-write):
  1) Tokenize incoming request text and run redaction regex rules.
  2) Replace matches with configured replacement ("[REDACTED]"), or store hashed value: hash(value) = sha256(value)[:16].
  3) Remove/block non-allowlisted headers.

- Example redaction regex (simple):
  - email: (?i)\b[\w.%+-]+@[\w.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}\b
  - ssn (US): \b\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}\b
  - cc (last 4 allowed): (?<=\b\d{12})(\d{4})\b -> replace with ****$1

- Trace IDs: we usually store a hashed/truncated value to allow grouping without exposing raw IDs. For example: stored_trace = sha256(trace_id)[:16].

- Retention & lifecycle: logs land in a customer-scoped S3 bucket with lifecycle rules. We can set a 90-day retention policy and verify purge. For Private deployments we can use your on-prem storage and your KMS.

- Encryption & access: AES-256 at rest, TLS in transit. KMS-managed keys; customer-managed KMS available in Private. Access to log objects is RBAC-limited and audited.

- Sample config snippet (attached as YAML). You can enable sampling to reduce volume (e.g., sample_rate: 0.1 for only 10% of requests), or enable full capture for a specific route/model.

- Sample redacted log: attached sample_redacted_log.txt shows a request with PII fields replaced by [REDACTED] and a hashed trace id.

If you want, we can provide a short script to run your example payloads through our redaction engine and return a redacted sample.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
